UBS Profit Climbs as Wealth-Management Inflows Increase
UBS Group reported a rise in third-quarter net profit, boosted by growth in its wealth-management platform.

The Swiss banking group said net profit for the third quarter was $2.69 billion, up from $2.48 billion in the year-earlier period. The figure was lower than analysts' expectations of $2.71 billion, according to consensus estimates compiled by the bank.

UBS said its results were helped by the addition of $55.1 billion of net new assets in global wealth management, representing a 4.5% annualized growth rate. UBS noted particularly strong inflows in the Asia Pacific region and the Americas.
Revenue grew to $13.35 billion from $12.76 billion. This exceeded expectations of $13.10 billion, according to the same consensus.
UBS said investor sentiment remains measured as the bank enters the fourth quarter. It expects a "more typical sequential seasonal moderation" in transaction volumes across its businesses.

The bank expects fourth-quarter net interest income to increase by a low-single-digit percentage sequentially in global wealth management and increase slightly in personal and corporate banking in Swiss-franc terms.
